/**
 * Server-side SFTP proxy for the in-portal file manager.
 *
 * This is a plain (non-"use server") module so it can be imported by both the
 * server actions (lib/actions-files.ts) and the upload/download route handler.
 * It never runs in the browser — the customer's root credentials stay on the
 * server; the browser only ever talks to our own actions/route.
 *
 * Connection target is derived EXACTLY like the server detail page:
 *   - dedicated-IP servers connect to their own IP on port 22
 *   - NAT servers use PUBLIC_IP + the forwarded SSH port
 * Username is always "root"; password is `server.rootPassword`.
 *
 * SANDBOX: on staging (NXEON_SANDBOX=1) no real SSH connection is ever opened —
 * every op is backed by a small in-memory simulated filesystem so the whole
 * file-manager UX works end to end without a live VM.
 */
import SftpClient from "ssh2-sftp-client";
import { SANDBOX } from "./sandbox";
import { decryptSecret } from "./crypto-box";

/**
 * Resolve a server's plaintext root password, preferring the encrypted-at-rest
 * value and falling back to the legacy plaintext column for rows that predate
 * encryption. Every READ of a root password must go through this helper so both
 * shapes keep working transparently.
 */
export function serverRootPassword(
  server: { rootPassword: string | null; rootPasswordEnc?: string | null }
): string | null {
  return decryptSecret(server.rootPasswordEnc) ?? server.rootPassword;
}

/** The minimal shape of a Server we need to open a connection. */
export type SftpServer = {
  id: string;
  rootPassword: string | null;
  rootPasswordEnc?: string | null;
  sshPort: number | null;
  dedicatedIp?: { address: string } | null;
};

export type SftpEntry = {
  name: string;
  /** "d" directory, "-" file, "l" symlink, etc. (ssh2-sftp-client `type`). */
  type: string;
  isDirectory: boolean;
  size: number;
  /** Unix mtime in ms. */
  modifiedMs: number;
  /** Numeric permission bits (e.g. 0o644), or null if unknown. */
  mode: number | null;
};

export type SftpStat = {
  isDirectory: boolean;
  size: number;
  modifiedMs: number;
  mode: number | null;
};

const CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;

/** Max length for any absolute path we accept from the client. */
export const MAX_PATH_LEN = 4096;
/** Max length for a single path segment (file/folder name). */
export const MAX_NAME_LEN = 255;

/**
 * Normalize + validate an absolute POSIX path coming from the browser. Rejects
 * relative paths, `..` traversal, NUL bytes, and over-long paths. Returns a
 * cleaned absolute path (collapsed slashes, resolved `.`), always starting with
 * "/". Throws on anything suspicious — callers surface the message.
 */
export function normalizePath(input: string): string {
  if (typeof input !== "string") throw new Error("Invalid path.");
  if (input.length > MAX_PATH_LEN) throw new Error("Path is too long.");
  if (input.includes("\0")) throw new Error("Invalid path.");
  if (!input.startsWith("/")) throw new Error("Path must be absolute.");

  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const part of input.split("/")) {
    if (part === "" || part === ".") continue;
    if (part === "..") throw new Error("Path traversal is not allowed.");
    if (part.length > MAX_NAME_LEN) throw new Error("A path segment is too long.");
    out.push(part);
  }
  return "/" + out.join("/");
}

/**
 * Validate a single new file/folder name — no slashes, no traversal, no NUL,
 * not "." or "..". Returns the name unchanged if valid.
 */
export function validateName(name: string): string {
  if (typeof name !== "string" || name.length === 0) throw new Error("A name is required.");
  if (name.length > MAX_NAME_LEN) throw new Error("Name is too long.");
  if (name.includes("/") || name.includes("\0")) throw new Error("Name contains invalid characters.");
  if (name === "." || name === "..") throw new Error("That name is not allowed.");
  return name;
